title: fix: USB hotplug callback does not validate device descriptor fields before slot_add
description:
In src/wp11_pkcs11.c, the hotplug callback (~line 650-655) calls libusb_get_device_descriptor() and uses desc.idVendor and desc.idProduct without validating the descriptor struct's own fields (bLength, bDescriptorType).

Per USB spec, a valid device descriptor has: bLength == 18 (sizeof(libusb_device_descriptor)) and bDescriptorType == 0x01 (LIBUSB_DT_DEVICE). A malformed or incomplete descriptor with arbitrary idVendor/idProduct values could in theory match a token_db entry — though this is low-likelihood on a local USB bus.

More practically: after the token_db lookup succeeds, the device is added to a slot and a CCID open is attempted. If the device descriptor is malformed (wrong bNumConfigurations, missing bcdUSB field), the CCID open will fail — but the slot is already allocated and partially initialized.

Fix:
1. After libusb_get_device_descriptor() returns 0, validate: desc.bDescriptorType == LIBUSB_DT_DEVICE (0x01) and desc.bLength == 18
2. Validate desc.idVendor != 0 (vendor ID 0 is not assigned per USB-IF)
3. These checks go before the token_db_lookup call
4. Add comment: 'Validate descriptor type before trusting VID/PID — malformed descriptors can match arbitrary entries.'

This closes the gap between 'hotplug fires' and 'slot is trusted'.
